body:
N-26 SLICE 4, PART 2, FOR THE LEAD TO DECIDE: THE LIVE CREDIT "<Artist>, live at <Venue> - <Channel>" (THE ARTE TITLE) IS NOT BUILT, BECAUSE THE NEGATIVE CORPUS REFUSES IT (helper-n26s4, 15 Nov 2026). The acceptance criterion is "a rule is accepted only if NO negative row changes"; I did not drop or reclassify the row to reach 0.

THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE: "Bohemian Rhapsody, live at Wembley - Queen" on the channel Queen (or Queen Official) reads right today (artist Queen, flagged channel). It has the SAME features as "Sepultura, live at Hellfest Open Air 2026 - ARTE Concert": a left side "<X>, live at <V>" and a right side that is the uploader's whole name. No rule that reads only the title and the uploader can file the second under Sepultura without filing the first under "Bohemian Rhapsody" (and "Hey Jude, live at Hyde Park - Paul McCartney" under "Hey Jude"). A test shows the two families have identical features. Giving the new reading basis channel would flag it weak, but the artist shown would still be a song's name. So today the ARTE title stays as slice 1 left it: under ARTE Concert, flagged channel, never given a picture or an artist page (leftover rows, owner: your decision, then N-28).

OPTIONS: (1) Accept the counter-example: read the left side as the artist with basis channel. Four hand rows change from the performer to a song name (flagged weak, no picture or page); N-28 can upgrade. Cost: a visibly wrong artist name for a performer's own "Song, live at V - Performer" upload. (2) A discriminator from OUTSIDE the title: the entry's length. The two recorded ARTE entries of this form run 50:08 and 59:29 (full shows); a song uploaded by its own performer runs minutes. Both readers already have the duration; read_upload does not take it yet; it needs a threshold and its own recorded rows (size S, a signature change in uploads.py and readers.py only). Fragile at the edges (a 20-minute live EP). (3) Leave it to N-28: the catalogue names the artist of a channel song by its title. Nothing is wrong in the library meanwhile except one flagged channel name.

MY VIEW: (2) is the proper fix if you want it in this slice, after recording at least ten "Song, live at V - Artist" titles with their lengths from artists' own channels (the corpus must contain them before the threshold is chosen); (3) is the honest state until then. (1) trades a flagged-right name for a flagged-wrong one and I would not take it. I stopped here: the choice is yours and nothing else in the slice depends on it.
